findings.title: Module lint test classification is wider than the build exclusion and the vitest include. apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts:177 sets TEST_FILE = /\.test\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/, and :461 isTest = TEST_FILE.test(file) grants the test allowances: :471 import of the composition-root files modules.ts / architecture.testkit.ts, and :480 import of vitest. But apps/api/tsconfig.build.json:10 excludes only src/**/*.test.ts, *.test.tsx and *.testkit.ts, and vitest.config.ts:21 collects only apps/api/src/**/*.test.ts. So a module file named *.test.mts / .test.cts (also .test.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx) is never run as a test, is compiled into dist, yet gets test-only exemptions from the boundary check. This is introduced by the F-DG1-134 fix (e71f3d0), and architecture.test.ts:763 pins the behaviour as intended. It is not a regression: before the fix such files were not scanned at all.
findings.reproduction: Candidate sha256:00f1498c...c80b, full disposable clone at 08cbd12, Node v22.22.2, after pnpm -r build. I planted apps/api/src/modules/kpi/zzgap.test.mts containing `import { API_MODULES } from "../../modules.ts"; export const moduleCount: number = Object.keys(API_MODULES).length;`. Results: (1) moduleViolations("kpi") = 0. (2) cd apps/api && pnpm build exits 0, and dist/modules/kpi/ contains zzgap.test.mjs (+ .d.mts). (3) node: import("./dist/modules/kpi/zzgap.test.mjs") gives moduleCount = 13, so it runs from the production artefact. (4) `vitest list --project unit-node` lists it 0 times, so it is not a test. (5) Control: the same content as zzgap.mts gives `modules/kpi/zzgap.mts: imports ../../modules.ts outside src/modules (composition root)`. The same exemption also admits `import ... from "vitest"` (a devDependency). Rules 1-5 (banned names, computed keys, runtime roots, syntax, node:crypto named-only) still apply to such files: the exemption is only the 2 composition-root files + vitest. Logs: docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/code-security/round-13/03-test-name-allowance-gap.log and 01-F-DG1-134-reproof-probe.log (GAP probe case).
findings.expected: A module file gets test allowances only if it is really a test: excluded from the build AND collected by vitest. Either narrow TEST_FILE to the extensions the build excludes and vitest runs (today .test.ts; .test.tsx is excluded from the build and so also harmless), or widen tsconfig.build.json `exclude` (and, if wanted, the vitest include) to src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}. architecture.test.ts:763 should assert the chosen invariant, for example that a *.test.mts which the build would emit gets no exemption.
findings.actual: A production-shipped module file named *.test.mts (or .test.cts/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx) may import apps/api/src/modules.ts, apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts (which tsc then pulls into the build, dragging in the typescript devDependency) and vitest with 0 lint violations, though it is never run as a test.

history.note: Raised by code-security-reviewer in DG1 round 13 while verifying the F-DG1-134 fix. Rated Low and non-mandatory: the exemption reaches only the declarative module map (data, no capability), the test-only lint and vitest. Rules 1-5 still apply to the file, so no loader, native or crypto-enumeration route opens. No access-control, integrity, calculation or portability impact. The lint is static defence-in-depth over human-reviewed code. Exploitation needs a contributor to commit an unusually named file past review, and the real tree has none. Same precedent as F-DG1-134/132/130. Proposed ID F-DG1-135 (next free number in the code-security 1xx range); the orchestrator may renumber. Does not block DG1.
